image_description: A close-up, high-angle photograph of a Triceratops skull and partial skeletal mount in a museum setting. The image focuses heavily on the cranium, showcasing the three horns (two brow, one nasal) and the large bony frill. The rest of the skeleton is visible in the background but is out of focus or partially cropped. The lighting is warm and artificial.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic triceratops horn configuration: two large supraorbital horns curving forward/upward and a smaller nasal horn. They are structurally sound and correctly positioned relative to the eye sockets.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rostral bone (beak core) is visible at the front of the skull. It has the characteristic hooked, parrot-like shape. While the keratin sheath is missing (as it is a skeleton), the underlying bone structure matches the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a close-up of the head. The limbs are either completely out of frame or too blurred/obscured by the angle and depth of field to verify their 'columnar' or 'elephant-like' nature. Marking as untestable to avoid hallucination.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill is the dominant feature behind the horns. It extends significantly backward and appears wide. The perspective confirms it is a large, shield-like structure attached to the posterior of the skull.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (not fenestrated like Chasmosaurus). The surface texture is consistent with fossilized bone. There are visible undulations along the margin that correspond to epoccipitals.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a skeletal mount; no skin, scales, or soft tissue are present. This checkpoint is inherently untestable for this specific image modality.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body and limb proportions are not visible due to the tight crop on the head. Cannot verify the slope of the back.
The tail is completely outside the frame.

artifact_observations.location: Right side of the frill (viewer's right)
artifact_observations.reasoning: The edge of the frill on the right side appears to have a jagged, unnatural break or fusion with the background shadow. It lacks the clean, defined edge of a fossil bone, looking slightly 'melted' or digitally eroded rather than naturally broken.

artifact_observations.location: Nasal horn base and eye socket area
artifact_observations.reasoning: The texture transitions between the horn base and the skull roof are slightly blurry and lack the fine porous detail expected in high-res fossil photography. It has a slight 'waxy' or over-smoothed AI-generated appearance.

The background elements (presumably the rest of the skeleton) seem to warp slightly into the wall/floor boundary. The geometry of the supporting armature under the jaw is ambiguous and doesn't follow clear physical logic.
